free_tier.stated: Free: '$0 / forever', '2 files a day, up to 512 MB each', 'Standard hosts only'.

per_object_cap.stated: 512 MB per file on the free tier; no per-link cap is published for a paid plan

retention.stated: not applicable: links are generated on demand

egress.terms: Billed per byte: '$0.50 per GB on standard hosts', plus hosts count x3. Plans carry a monthly quota - Pro 15 GB/month, Premium 40 GB/month - with overage at $0.40 and $0.30/GB. A per-host daily bandwidth is also published for five hosts.
egress.free_allowance: Pro 15 GB/month, Premium 40 GB/month; pay-as-you-go credits from $2

interface_detail: No public API documentation was found: /api answers 404. The service is a web flow, and the per-host table is published as an HTML status page.
tooling: No documented API, no rclone backend; automation would need a browser session. That is a note about tooling, not a verdict.
chaining: The only service here that prices egress per byte, so it can absorb a one-off overflow when a capped host blocks elsewhere on a flat-rate plan.

limits.value: Pro 15 GB/month, Premium 40 GB/month, overage USD 0.40-0.30/GB
512 MB per file on the free tier
per host per day: NitroFlare 100 GB, FileBoom 50 GB, Keep2Share 50 GB, Upstore 20 GB, FileJoker 15 GB

limits_note: The status table has a Daily bandwidth column for 61 hosts and only 5 carry a number; the rest print an em dash, which the vendor leaves undefined.
binding_note: the plan quota binds about 27x before any host cap does.

identity_cost.detail: Not read: no signup form was opened. Free plan needs no payment; credits are bought with a card.

reliability_note: Five hosts are marked 'Partner network' rather than 'Own account', and two Plus hosts (FileJoker, Upstore) have 'never' in the last-checked column, so the published cap is a policy figure rather than an observed one for those.
confidence_note: Both tables are the vendor's own pages read today. The 5 published caps are policy statements; a paid download would be needed to confirm enforcement.

evidence.proved: 61-row table with Host, Availability, Served by, Status, 7-day success, Class, Daily bandwidth; 5 numeric caps, the rest em dash
